title: The Eternal Autumn
subtitle: O golden hue, no longer a gift from the Sun, nor a symbol of the harvest.

trails.title: Behind the Golden Famine
trails.description: Tragedy births poetry, yet he wishes there were no tragedies left to write.

content.text: A Poem Written on a Riverside Tree Trunk

Weeping Wheat

Glittering golden plains
A gentle breeze passes, yet no grain dances
The earth is like a misunderstood mother
Again and again
Reaching out her withered hands

I see sunlight fall on the fields
The wheat stands quiet and clean, almost cruel
O weeping wheat!
May you bear silent fruit, enough to sustain.
Even if only enough to fill a child's smile

—Anonymous poet, wandering along the Don

items.text: The Eternal Autumn
Tent, Sich
Downstream of the Don, on a stretch of flat meadow, a camp rises from mud-packed earth and stacked logs. It's no grand fortress, but it's enough to shelter an army at rest.
Zeno cavalry commander Ivan Ivanovich Burakov stands, tall and broad, watching the recruits drill their formations.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Commander.
With her usual brief greeting, Zeno cavalry chief of staff Sabina Sternova approaches.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Yes, Sabina?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: You've left the war room. Any commands?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Just catching a breath. That stuffy air will be the death of me.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Besides, a little more time among the pups won't hurt. Keep their spines straight and their commanding officer's face in their minds.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: I think they know your face already. After all, many only joined the cavalry after you gave that speech in the village.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Ah, Tamarovka. Tell me, Sabina, did the pups bring any news?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: From Ms. Galina? She's fine. She says she wants to see you again at your convenience.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: There are no great rides ahead for now. I'll find the time to visit her.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: *sigh* If this Golden Famine continues to gnaw at us, the Don will be no home for her.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: No winter, no crops ... The steppe has turned her most brutal. I will find a way to persuade her to leave.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: We reported the famine to the Foundation long ago, but there's still no sign of their investigators.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: This is far from the heart of the war, and with the Foundation so short on manpower, we're just dust on their boots.
Messy hoofbeats burst from the camp entrance—the familiar sound of bad news.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: What's wrong?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Out of the way, rookies. Wounded incoming.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Yeah, don't you hear his whimpering? I could almost cry.
At the rear, tied to a horse's back, sits a wailing injured boy.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Sh-Shut up, Sasha! I got shot, for God's sake, shot!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Argh, it hurts. I'm never going to walk again.
The soldiers quickly clear the way for the reconnaissance team. Lilya dismounts first, followed by the rest of the team, except Sergey.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: Leave Sergey to me, Lieutenant. You should report to the commander.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: On it. And find a way to shut him up before the whole camp's forced to listen to the wails of his great military feat.
She turns to see the commander striding forward.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: No need to hunt me down, Lieutenant. What news?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Bad is what. Broomstick's broken. Won't be flying until I get the parts to fix it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But it gets worse. We have a situation, sir. And I think it's a big one.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: To the war room. You too, Sabina.
Commander's Tent, Sich

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: So, the bandits have Zeno AZP-37s and arcane-guided VT fuse anti-aircraft guns.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You swear it, Lieutenant?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Yes. We practiced how to dodge anti-aircraft shots with these kinds of guns when I was a trainee. Loaded with training ammo, of course.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: There have been no reports of missing weapons, and we're not carrying any AZPs.
The chief of staff, keeping the entire supply chain in mind, quickly rules out several possibilities.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Then those weapons came from an outer source, and like as not, they have more of them.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: An outer source ... Impossible through air, and all land and water routes are under our surveillance.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: And there's no reason the locals wouldn't know about any hidden bypaths they might have used.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: I can't think of any way of transporting mass weaponry and personnel without drawing attention.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Then we look to the hand that fed them. Who would hold Zeno weaponry besides Zeno itself?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Manus Vindictae? They might've captured them on another battlefield and given them to the bandits here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Yeah, the Manus. That would save us some brain juice. But I don't think that's likely.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Do you know how many humans there are among the bandits? Any Manus would blast them all to bits before they gave them so much as a pistol.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Plus, these guys ran as soon as they suffered a loss. There's no way they're under Manus Vindictae's control.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: There is a possibility we're ignoring here: Igor's rebels.
For a second, the faces of the Cavalry Corps's leaders freeze. Even the candlelight seems to stop flickering. Only Lilya seems immune to it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You served under Igor, didn't you, Commander? He's more than capable of transporting personnel and supplies in unconventional ways, right?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: I have to correct you, Lieutenant.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You're right. While under Igor, I saw his arcane skill in use. He could slip men and guns through stone as if it were air.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Well, good news is, Igor cut ties with Manus Vindictae after the ritual in Antarctica. So whether it's him or them, we only need to deal with one.
News like this cannot lift the iron-gray shadows sitting beneath the commander's eyes.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: If it is Igor, the questions only grow. Why bring this Gryphon Legion of his to Bereggrad, so far from the front?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Even if he seeks something here, why ride with bandits? He never stomached their filth before.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Is it supplies he wants? But the Golden Famine grips the entire basin. Or is this all by his hand?
His questions quickly trail off into agitated muttering. He stops himself before more can leave his lips.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I'll send word to headquarters. Intelligence should reach a more solid conclusion.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Sabina, double the patrols. I want eyes on the woods at all times.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Yes, sir.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Lieutenant Lilya, since horsemanship is not your expertise, you will remain at camp until your broomstick is mended. That's an order.
Lilya almost defends her riding skills but quickly swallows her words.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Alright, understood.
It's easy to find the field kitchen at this hour. The aroma of hot unleavened bread guides their rumbling stomachs through the maze of tents.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Right in time for dinner.
She glances at Sergey, who's standing among the other soldiers around a huge soup pot. He holds his bowl, talking between heavy mouthfuls.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: ... In that moment, I saw the bullet coming at me! I'm telling you, my amulet worked!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Gave me just enough time to dodge the hit to the chest. Still hit the leg, though. You have no idea how much it hurts.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Too bad it didn't hit your mouth.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: H-Hey, Lieutenant.
His legs snap to attention, some cabbage soup spilling from the bowl in his quivering hand onto his fingertips.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh yeah, must really hurt. Still managed to drag yourself to the mess hall for some soup though, didn't you?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: W-Well, of course! It'll take more than a bullet to take me down. Speaking of soup—
He raises the bowl in his hand. Inside, a few measly scraps of cabbage float around a single soaked scrap of bread.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Look at this stuff! We're soldiers, not rabbits!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Quit your whining. I know you've got some dried meat. Eat it.
Lilya grabs a piece of bread from the table and spoons herself a bowl of soup. The thin cabbage leaves sink to the bottom of the bowl like damp gauze.
Like everyone else, she dips the dry unleavened bread into her soup to soften it.
Sergey hands her some dried meat, then pulls a bottle from behind his back. The liquid inside is clear—seemingly harmless.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Here, have some, Lieutenant.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Not bad.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: So, what was it? How come the bandits have something powerful enough to shoot you down?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Don't know how, don't know why. Nobody does.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Well, it isn't hard to guess. They're obviously going to rob the villages! Wait. This is bad. All the young and fit have gone to war. They won't be able to defend themselves.
For a moment, a dark cloud falls upon his face. But soon, it's lightened by another idea.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hey, no orders this afternoon, right? Want to go fishing with me? I'm going to the river.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Now? You forget that bullet so quick?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: I know a safe place where we can fish, and I've got the amulet! There's no bullet that can kill me. Trust me.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: You're not going to tell me you're full after that sorry excuse for a soup, are you? There may not be any crops, but I bet there are still plenty of fish in the river.
Lilya checks Sergey's allegedly shot leg.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Weren't you just wailing about your leg a few hours ago?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: It-It's no big deal!
He finishes the last of his food, drops the bowl, and jogs away.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: "Shot in the leg." Pft. More like scratched.
Field, Steppe
The arid wind blows the needlegrass into a sea of rustling waves.

items.speaker: Andreas
items.text: Neigh—
A horse's playground. But for a fugitive on a long run from the authorities, it's hell.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *sigh* Charon, how far have we gone since we left the road?
On the open grassland, one might travel for hours without seeing another soul. Among the endless waves of grass, it's easy to lose your way.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Fifteen kilometers southeast, perhaps less. Our speed is slower than usual.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Are you weary? Would you like to rest?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Um, maybe later. This doesn't seem like the best place for a break. Do you think this map is reliable? The one the cart driver gave us?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The cart driver?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Alright, I'll refresh your memory one more time, or should I say, for the millionth time.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It all started after we left Poland. Somehow, we got ourselves on a train heading east—the one full of Czechoslovakians.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Memories of you insisting they let us aboard the train because "you can avoid the soldiers in black in the East" come to mind.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Of course you'd remember that of all things. Anyway, so we got on the train, but before we could get too far, it was stopped by some group.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: A fight must've broken out, because there were gunshots everywhere. It was utter bedlam, so we grabbed Andreas from the stock car and slipped away south.

items.speaker: Andreas
items.text: Neigh ...
The warhorse seems grateful for the daring rescue.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: That's when we met the cart driver I mentioned. He'd lost a horse.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So we made a deal: we'd lend him Andreas for the day, and he'd take us somewhere safe.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Then he has fulfilled his promise. This is indeed a peaceful and safe place.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Hardly! We're in the middle of bloody nowhere! If we can't find people soon, we'll—no, I'll—starve to death!
Charon lowers his head, troubled by his failure to consider the needs of the living. Andreas also turns his head aside. He can live off the grassland alone.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Oh, n-not to blame you two. *sigh* Forget it. Guess there's nothing for it but to keep moving forwards.
She lifts the messy, hand-drawn map again, squinting to make out the shape of a river among its chaotic lines.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: He said we could find his niece in Perevoznaya by the Don River. But which one is the Don?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *sigh* If we're even going in the right direction, that is, or if this map is actually accurate. Um, Andreas?

items.speaker: Andreas
items.text: Neigh?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Could I stand on your back for a minute?
Andreas lowers himself, allowing the girl to clamber onto his back.
Then, they both rise at the same time, Merel's feet trembling.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: What are you doing, Merel? You could fall.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I-I'm fine. Just be ready to *grunt* catch me if I fall, alright?
Merel shakily detaches the telescope she picked up in some ruins from her belt and looks toward what she believes to be the east.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Where could it be? All I see is grass and trees.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Alright, other side, other side. *gasp*

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Ch-Charon! Charon, I see rooftops! Right ahead! You—

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Wah! Help!
She hops in excitement and, as expected, loses her balance.
